title: The economic impact of the UK's beer and pub industry
gist: Oxford Economics, commissioned by the British Beer and Pub Association, estimates the UK beer and pub industry generated £37.8bn of GVA and supported almost 1 million jobs in 2025, with 711,300 direct employees — 48% of them aged 16–24 versus 11% economy-wide.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics estimates the UK beer and pub industry generated a total of £37.8 billion in gross value added contributions to UK GDP in 2025.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Sizes the sector's political weight in fiscal debates over alcohol duty and business rates.

insights.claim: The UK beer and pub industry supported almost 1 million jobs and £21.2 billion of employee compensation in 2025, including indirect and induced effects.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Large labour footprint makes the sector sensitive to minimum-wage and employer-NIC changes — a margin watchpoint for UK pub groups and brewers.

insights.claim: The UK beer and pub sector directly employed 711,300 people in 2025, generating £18.6 billion in direct GVA and £11.7 billion in employee compensation.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Direct GVA per employee is low (~£26k), signalling a labour-intensive, low-margin industry exposed to wage-cost inflation.

insights.claim: 341,900 workers aged 16–24 were employed in the UK beer and pub industry in 2025 — 48% of the sector's direct employment, versus 11% across the UK economy.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Heavy reliance on young, part-time workers makes UK hospitality a bellwether for youth unemployment and acutely exposed to youth minimum-wage rises.
insights.locator: The beer and pub sector provides a vital source

insights.claim: The British Beer and Pub Association commissioned the Oxford Economics study, which covers brewing, pubs, the beer-attributable share of the rest of the on-trade, and beer-dependent off-trade, down to local authority and constituency level.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Industry-commissioned impact numbers are lobbying inputs; treat totals as advocacy-grade upper bounds when sizing policy risk.
insights.locator: To understand the current scale of its economic footprint
